hook: SCP-8411 is a short catalogue of symbols found on birch trees across the Appalachians, and nearly all of its weight sits in the final table. The symbols themselves are shown as images, but each entry also gives the meaning it conveys, so the list works fine as text. Take it slowly, from top to bottom.
whyItMatters: It is a lean example of building dread through a list: no narrative and no interviews, just fifteen rows that drift from practical trail advice toward something else. The idea that many different hands left these marks across the mountains, and that anyone who searches for them long enough starts to read them, suggests a hidden shared language in the woods. It is telling that the people who can read them are search-and-rescue teams, security and containment staff.
thingsToNotice: The first entries are the sort of thing a hunter or hiker might really carve: a tree stand, a safe zone, dangerous animals nearby, hunters welcome near the cabins. Midway the warnings begin assuming something else is out there, telling you not to search for someone who vanished, to ignore sounds, to check your count, and that something won't stay dead for long. The last rows stop giving advice and start announcing a presence: something listening, something watching, and finally a name, She Who Sees Through Trees. The line about trees having eyes at the very top of the page points straight at that final entry.
